newsitem.title: UK: Moody's examines MG effect on Deutsche.
newsitem.headline: Moody's examines MG effect on Deutsche.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service is looking at the implications for Deutsche Bank's ratings from the situation regarding Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, a Moody's banking analyst said on Monday.
"I can tell you we are looking at the situation," Samuel Theodore, managing director for European financial institutons at Moody's in London, told Reuters.
He said the rating agency's analysis was "in the general context of the rating for the group".
Deutsche Bank currently has an Aaa rating from Moody's and is one of the few triple-A rated banks in the world.
But in July Moody's revised its outlook on the German banking giant down to negative from stable, reflecting pressure on the bank's earnings.
Moody's said at the time Deutsche faced lower lending yields, tighter competition, flattening loan demand, rising costs and risks entailed in its aggressive expansion into investment banking.
Theodore said the bank's efforts to expand had been a key reason for the outlook change.
"We perceived this effort by the group to diversify as one area of potential risk," he told Reuters.
Deutsche Bank said on Monday that Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) had enough cash to cover fund outflows.

Trading in three of its funds was temporarily halted last week due to "irregularities". The manager of two of the funds, Peter Young, has been suspeneded and his personal assets frozen pending a probe into his management of the funds.
Salomon Brothers said in a research note on Monday that Deutsche's expansion into global investment banking highlighted its vulnerability to a credit downgrade.

"The reversion to its accident-prone image of the early 1990s comes at an awkward time: a rapid expansion into global investment banking has already raised Deutsche Bank's risk profile and, by extension, its vulnerability to a credit downgrade," the research note said.
